title: I built a mobile game on my phone while putting my kids to bed…
author: Slickabaut
selftext:
About 9 months ago, I started messing around with the idea of making a game, entirely from my phone at night while putting my kids to bed.

I’ve always loved games. I actually worked at Blizzard Entertainment for many years, although on the business side, never as a game developer.  
I’ve gotten pretty hooked on vibe coding over the past couple of years. I built a construction-related product that helped me land a job, along with a bunch of other tools and demos. But I’d always wanted to make a game, and not being a programmer or an artist made that pretty difficult until AI came along.

I wanted to make something specifically for portrait-mode mobile play, since that’s about the only gaming I have time for these days.

What started as an experiment turned into about six months of development, almost entirely from my phone. My process was basically **play, debug, edit, adjust, repeat**. Every mechanic, animation, transition, button placement… probably far more polishing than necessary. Apparently I picked up a little of Blizzard’s philosophy along the way… 

The result is **Doomfall**, a turn-based artillery game with destructible terrain, ridiculous weapons, AI opponents, and a full league system with seasons (career) and playoffs.

I also discovered that one of the hardest parts of vibe coding is resisting the temptation to start another project. It’s so easy to explore a new idea, but after investing months into something, you almost feel guilty working on anything else. I’ve already got a few other games in various stages of development!

Anyway, **Doomfall is finally on the App Store!**

It’s completely free. **No ads, no in-app purchases, nothing to buy.** Just something fun I made with my kids, and a pretty cool experience going from an idea on my phone to an actual game people can play.

It’s certainly not perfect, but I’m glad I finally shipped it.

https://apps.apple.com/us/app/doomfall/id6827248017

Thank you for any feedback.
